name: 京町恋しぐれ 新宿 本館 (Kyomachi Koishigure Shinjuku Honkan)

claims.text: The restaurant's specialty dish list includes 生麩 (namafu / wheat gluten cake) as a featured Kyoto-style item, indicating wheat gluten is a core ingredient used in the kitchen rather than something avoided.

claims.text: Core matcha lattes are built from matcha powder, milk, and naturally gluten-free flavor add-ins like kuromitsu, kinako, and houjicha, with no dashi or soy-sauce-based savory dishes on the menu to introduce hidden wheat or fish stock.

claims.text: The mazesoba tare is described as soy-sauce (shoyu) based, which in standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat; no wheat-free tamari alternative was mentioned.
The signature tare is a shoyu (soy sauce)-based sauce aged for about a week; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, and no wheat-free tamari or GF alternative is mentioned in any source.

name: 麺堂にしき 新宿歌舞伎町店 (Mendo Nishiki Shinjuku Kabukicho)

name: 麺屋武蔵 武骨外伝 (Menya Musashi Bukotsu Gaiden)

claims.text: The black-style dipping broth is finished with a special soy-sauce-based tare (paste), a wheat-containing seasoning typical of shoyu-style ramen.
The tsukemen noodles are made with wheat flour and the dipping broth is a conventional soy-sauce-seasoned pork-bone and seafood stock — no gluten-free noodle or broth alternative is documented.
The signature dipping broth combines pork-bone stock with bonito, mackerel, and dried-sardine (niboshi) fish stock, so both the tsukemen and ramen broths are animal-based with no vegan version noted.
